clue.text: City securing ties, say, with unskilful player

indicators.note: the word say marks that the tying phrase before it counts only as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: securing ties is knotting them
a ham is an overacting, unskilled performer

explanation.surface: A city clinches a deal on its fixtures with the help of a poor footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you KNOTTING is only heard: drop the silent K to get NOTTING. 'Ties' tempts as football fixtures; here they are knots.
explanation.definitionFit: Nottingham is an English city in the East Midlands.

clue.text: Destroyed, say, an African lake

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of say an are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An African lake has supposedly been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyed' rearranges SAYAN; ', say,' looks like a link here but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Nyasa, now Lake Malawi, is one of the great lakes of East Africa.

clue.text: People who reveal legends of famous archer?

parts.note: William Tell is the legendary Swiss crossbowman
legends are tales

explanation.surface: Those who spread stories about William Tell are passing on legends.
explanation.definitionFit: Telltales are sneaks who disclose others' secrets or wrongdoing.

clue.text: Upside-down, butterflies make marks on paper

parts.note: something upside-down has been inverted
the comma is a European butterfly with a white comma-shaped mark on its wing

explanation.surface: Butterflies leave marks when they land the wrong way up on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverted commas are quotation marks written or printed on a page.

clue.text: Puccini, perhaps, joining soldier on a lake in Italy

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
Como is a lake in northern Italy

explanation.surface: The composer Puccini joins an American serviceman on an Italian lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' says Puccini is one example of someone with this first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer of La Boheme was christened Giacomo Puccini.

clue.text: Dangerous element of loveless scenario, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the remaining letters may be arranged another way
loveless means the scenario is stripped of love, the zero score O in tennis

explanation.surface: A loveless plot holds a hazardous ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' drops O (love, nil in tennis) from SCENARIO; 'possibly' rearranges SCENARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a toxic chemical element used historically as a poison.

clue.text: Secular US city infuriated church leaders

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, the American city

indicators.note: leaders means the opening letters of the two words infuriated and church

explanation.surface: A godless American city has enraged the heads of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means belonging to the laity rather than the clergy, hence non-religious.

clue.text: Fish found between a couple of rays

definitions.meaning: to fish with rod and line

definitions.text: found between a couple of rays
definitions.meaning: in geometry the space between two lines from a point is measured in degrees

explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with a line; an angle lies between two rays meeting at a vertex.

clue.text: Did this clipper never touch the bottom?

definitions.text: Did this clipper never touch the bottom?

parts.words: Did this clipper never touch the bottom?
parts.note: a famous sailing ship whose Scots name means a short shirt, one too short to reach the backside

explanation.walkthrough: A clipper is a fast sailing ship; Scots 'cutty sark' is a short chemise, from Burns's Tam o' Shanter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cutty Sark is the preserved tea clipper at Greenwich, named for a short shirt.

clue.text: Backing group in early European Song Contest

definitions.text: Backing group in early European Song Contest

parts.words: Backing group in early European Song Contest
parts.note: not pop backing singers but the medieval German guild poets who held formal song competitions

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Eurovision; the clue means the German craftsmen-poets of Wagner's opera, where a song contest decides the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Meistersingers were members of German guilds of poets and musicians from the 14th to 16th centuries.

clue.text: Everyone getting to university by means of deposits

parts.note: everyone is all of them
via means by way of or by means of

explanation.surface: Everybody gets into university by paying money down.
explanation.definitionFit: Alluvia are sediments of silt and sand laid down by rivers, the plural of alluvium.

clue.text: Skill of team-leader on sledge

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece set on another follows it, so the leader comes after the sledge

parts.note: a sleigh is a sledge drawn over snow
the leading letter of the word team

explanation.surface: The lead dog of a husky team shows its skill pulling a sledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places T after SLEIGH in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is dexterity or cunning skill, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: PM is following the example of almost nobody

parts.note: to do something after someone is to follow their example, as in named after

indicators.note: almost means the word for nobody is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: no one means nobody

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister copies hardly anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister but is post meridiem; 'almost' trims NO ONE to NOON.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, post meridiem, marks the hours after midday.

clue.text: Unwell, fast losing power

indicators.note: losing says the letter for power drops out of the word for fast

parts.note: speedy means fast
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone feeling poorly finds they have lost their speed and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes P from SPEEDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling seedy is an informal way of feeling slightly ill or off-colour.

clue.text: Old-fashioned church music's played so sweetly

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made anew, so the letters of old are reworked

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: In an old-fashioned church the music is played gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-fashioned' reads as one adjective, but split it: 'fashioned' is the anagram signal working on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolce is the Italian musical direction to play softly and tenderly, with a gentle tone.

clue.text: After all, one goes into social gathering for flirtation

indicators.note: goes into means the pair enters the word for social gathering

parts.note: a dance is a social gathering

indicators.note: after means the numeral for one comes behind the word all

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: After all, someone sneaks into a party looking for romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After all' reads as 'nevertheless', but 'After' is an indicator placing one behind the word all, and 'goes into' sends the pair inside the gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance is casual amorous play, light flirting.

clue.text: Band of archers to regroup

indicators.note: regroup asks for the letters of archers to to be rearranged into a new formation

explanation.surface: A company of bowmen reorganises its ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large band of musicians.

clue.text: Excellent tripe pie served up in 4's restaurant

indicators.note: served up in a down answer means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI
tripe and rot both mean nonsense
a tart is a pie

explanation.surface: Fine tripe and pie dishes are presented at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses AIROTTART as a whole in this down entry. 4 points to GIACOMO, an Italian name, hence an Italian eatery; tripe looks like food but means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a modest Italian restaurant, the kind an Italian like Giacomo would know.

clue.text: Misdirected lawsuit that has no hope of success

definitions.text: that has no hope of success

parts.note: something misdirected goes astray and is lost
a cause is a case brought before a court

explanation.surface: A lawsuit filed with the wrong court is doomed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost cause is a venture or campaign bound to fail.

clue.text: French one left port — with blank manifest, presumably

parts.note: un is French for one
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A French ship leaves harbour with nothing listed on its cargo papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship carrying no cargo has nothing on its manifest, so it is empty of freight.

clue.text: Painful result of English horse entering a race

indicators.note: entering means the letter for horse goes inside a race

parts.note: taken as written
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: An English horse comes to grief in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' looks like a racehorse but is H, heroin; 'entering' puts it in ARACE, before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: An earache is a pain in the ear, the consequence of infection or loud noise.

clue.text: Tin box of old that was hard to hunt down

definitions.text: that was hard to hunt down

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
ark is an old word for a chest or box

explanation.surface: An antique tin chest proved elusive to collectors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Snark is the elusive quarry of Lewis Carroll's poem The Hunting of the Snark; ark is an archaic word for a coffer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's nonsense poem tells of a crew's hopeless hunt for an imaginary creature.

clue.text: Vernacular I would use, going to holiday isle

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would
IOM is the Isle of Man, a holiday island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Someone says they'd adopt the local dialect when holidaying on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a form of expression peculiar to a language or its everyday speech.

clue.text: Valuable bar pub reportedly acquired

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for pub is judged by how it is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: an inn is a pub
got means acquired

explanation.surface: A bar owner reportedly bought a pub of great worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns INN into its sound-alike IN; 'bar' looks like a pub counter, but the definition's bar is of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a cast block of precious metal such as gold.

clue.text: Operatic spectacles held up by Handel, we hear

definitions.text: Operatic spectacles held up by Handel, we hear

parts.words: Operatic spectacles held up by Handel, we hear
parts.note: glasses for use at the opera, held up to the eyes not by the composer but by a handle, which Handel sounds like

explanation.surface: Opera productions are staged by the composer Handel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operatic spectacles' look like Handel's stage shows; they are opera glasses on a stick, held by a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of opera glasses held up to the eyes by a long side handle.

clue.text: Take steps to form alliance with running mate?

definitions.text: Take steps to form alliance with running mate?

parts.words: Take steps to form alliance with running mate?
parts.note: not a political ticket but a couple running off together to get married secretly

explanation.walkthrough: 'running mate' suggests a vice-presidential partner; here the running is fleeing and the alliance is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly in order to marry.

clue.text: Miser including two grand in tax return

indicators.note: including means the reversed word takes the two thousands inside it
return asks for the word meaning tax to be read backwards

parts.note: to drain or tax is to sap resources
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds, so two of them give GG

explanation.surface: A skinflint holds back two thousand pounds when filing his tax return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses the word for tax (giving NIARD), and 'including' puts the two grand inside it; a grand is a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggard is a stingy, ungenerous person, a skinflint.

clue.text: Drinking toast for so long

definitions.meaning: a cheery word said when raising glasses, like cheers
so long is an informal farewell, like bye-bye

explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is both an old toast and a casual British goodbye.

clue.text: Common grub found in wheat stalks

indicators.note: found in signals the answer lies inside the run of letters of wheat stalks

explanation.surface: Ordinary insect larvae live in the stems of wheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' suggests a larva in the stalks; it is slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal slang for food, just as grub is.

clue.text: Highway from Bury, say?

parts.note: to inter is to bury
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A main road leads out of the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the town in Greater Manchester, capitalised to mislead; it is the verb. Interstates are US motorways.
explanation.definitionFit: An interstate is a major US motorway linking several states.
